general.colorPaperHint: Warm cream, easy on the eyes
general.colorTokyonightHint: Blue-violet night, Tokyo Day when light
general.colorThemeHint: Every theme has a light and a dark version.
general.animatedBackgroundHint: Slow light behind the app that follows the agent’s state. Paused under reduced motion.
general.rowDensityHint: How much each row shows in the session list and the conductor's worker panel. Saved on this device only.
general.fontHint: Font of the whole app. "Theme font" keeps the colour theme's own. Code blocks keep their monospace font. Saved on this device only.
general.appFontSizeHint: Size of the app's text outside conversations (default 13 px). Only text grows; spacing stays. Saved on this device only.
general.chatFontSizeHint: Size of a session's answers (default 14 px); the rest of the conversation scales with it. Saved on this device only.
general.quitPolicyHint: Applies when sessions are running or processes are left over. "Keep" still stops sessions and Puppeteer helpers.
general.launchAtLoginHint: Starts Puppeteer when you log in. "Start minimized" keeps the window minimized (in the Dock or taskbar).

google.title: Google Account (Drive + Gmail + Calendar)
google.intro: Connect one or more Google accounts so the AI can work with your Drive files, Gmail and Calendar. Tools appear as mcp__google__* in four groups — drive_*, sheets_*, mail_* and cal_*; with multiple accounts the AI targets one via each tool's account argument (the default account when omitted). Write, delete, share and send actions still go through the permission prompt, and calendar attendees are never emailed unless the AI explicitly asks to notify them. Refresh tokens are stored in your OS Keychain (never written to disk). Takes effect on the next run.
google.credsWarning: Create your own OAuth Desktop app credentials in Google Cloud Console, enable the Drive API, Sheets API, Gmail API and Calendar API, then paste the Client ID and Secret below.
google.loginExpired: Google session expired or was revoked. Click "Login" to re-authorize.
google.missingScopes: This account is missing permissions ({scopes}) — it was connected before they were added, so some APIs (e.g. Calendar) return 401. Click "Login" to re-authorize.
google.loggingIn: Opening browser to sign in again…
google.credsSaved: OAuth credentials saved — no need to re-enter them.
google.enterLabel: Enter a label for the account (e.g. work, personal).
google.enterBothCreds: Enter both Client ID and Client Secret.
google.removeMessage: The AI will lose access to this account. Your saved OAuth credentials are kept so you can re-add it without re-entering them.
google.forgetMessage: This removes the stored Client ID/Secret and ALL connected accounts. You will need to paste the credentials again next time.

github.title: GitHub Accounts
github.intro: Add GitHub accounts once and link them to projects. PATs are stored securely in your OS Keychain (never written to disk). Required scopes: repo (private) or public_repo (public).
github.isolationWarning: Keep this machine logged out of gh globally: do not run gh auth login or set GH_TOKEN system-wide. Puppeteer wires the correct per-project credential at run time; a global login would let runs bypass that isolation.
github.patPlaceholder: New PAT (leave blank to keep current)
github.deleteMessage: Delete this GitHub account? Projects linked to it will be unlinked.

gitlab.title: GitLab Accounts
gitlab.intro: Add GitLab accounts once and link them to projects. PATs are stored securely in your OS Keychain (never written to disk). Set a custom host for self-hosted GitLab, and an optional commit email. Required scope: api (or read_api + write_repository) — a repository-only token is rejected by the validation endpoint.
gitlab.isolationWarning: Keep this machine logged out of glab globally: do not run glab auth login or set GITLAB_TOKEN system-wide. Puppeteer wires the correct per-project credential at run time; a global login would let runs bypass that isolation.
gitlab.patPlaceholder: New PAT (leave blank to keep current)
gitlab.deleteMessage: Delete this GitLab account? Projects linked to it will be unlinked.

aws.title: AWS Accounts
aws.intro: Add AWS accounts once and link one account to each project. Secret Access Keys and Session Tokens are stored securely in your OS Keychain. Puppeteer wires the selected project account to Claude and Codex runs through the broker.
aws.isolationWarning: Avoid setting AWS credentials globally for agent work. Puppeteer gates aws calls through its broker; credential/config mutation such as aws configure is blocked.
aws.ssoExpired: SSO token expired or not signed in. Click "SSO login" to sign in again.
aws.newSecretPlaceholder: New Secret Access Key (leave blank to keep current)
aws.sessionTokenReplacePlaceholder: Session Token (optional; set when replacing secret)
aws.profileAllAdded: All profiles from ~/.aws/config are already added
aws.ssoLoginNeeded: SSO token missing or expired — sign in to list accounts.
aws.ssoUseManual: Enter a profile name manually instead
aws.ssoUsePicker: Pick a role via SSO instead
aws.deleteMessage: Delete this AWS account? Projects linked to it will be unlinked.

claude.loginWaitingHint: Waiting for you to sign in in the browser…
claude.validNeedsLogin: Not logged in yet — click Login to authenticate
claude.deleteMessage: This removes the account from Puppeteer and unlinks it from any projects. Your global ~/.claude login is not affected.

balance.title: Auto-balance default
balance.hint: Automatically point the default at the least-used account so plan usage spreads evenly. New runs that aren't pinned to a project follow it; running/resumed runs keep their account.
balance.suggest: Suggestion: switch the default to {account} to balance usage.

accounts.intro: Sign in to several Claude (Pro/Max) and ChatGPT (Codex) subscriptions. Each account keeps its login in a profile of its own (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for Claude, CODEX_HOME for Codex), so sessions can run on different accounts side by side and a project can be linked to one account.
accounts.securityShort: Puppeteer never stores your passwords or tokens.
accounts.securityNote: Claude Code and Codex keep the login in the account's own profile; Puppeteer never stores the password or OAuth token. Adding or removing an account here never touches your global ~/.claude or ~/.codex login.
accounts.sharedCodexHint: The login in ~/.codex, made with codex login in a terminal. Codex sessions use it while no Codex account is the default.
accounts.deleteCodexMessage: This removes the account and its login from Puppeteer, and projects linked to it go back to the default. Your global ~/.codex login is not affected.

add.title: Add account
add.claudeDesc: A Claude subscription, for Claude sessions.
add.codexDesc: A ChatGPT plan, for Codex sessions.
add.claudeHint: Creates a profile for the account, then opens the browser to sign in to Claude with it.
add.codexHint: Creates a Codex home (CODEX_HOME) for the account, then runs codex login to sign in with ChatGPT in the browser.
add.cancelNote: Cancelling now removes this account, as it has not signed in yet.

login.deviceCode: Enter this code on the sign-in page
login.pasteCode: Page shows a code? Paste it here
login.useDeviceCode: Browser can't reach Puppeteer? Use a device code instead
login.notSignedIn: The sign-in ended, but the account is still not signed in.

ai.sessionDefaultsHint: What a new session starts with, unless it picks its own.
ai.fallbackHint: Takes over a turn while the Claude model is overloaded or unavailable; the next turn tries the model again. Its usage and limits apply to that turn.
ai.reloadCodexModelsTitle: Refresh the model list from the Codex CLI (codex debug models)
ai.validateModelsTitle: Run a one-word turn on each model to see which ones your Claude account still serves (uses a little quota)
ai.validateHint: Not checked yet — click Validate to see which models your account still serves.
ai.validateRunning: Checking each model against your account…
ai.validateError: Validation failed — could not run the check.
ai.modelsRefreshError: Refresh failed — keeping the last cached list.
ai.codexRefreshHint: Not refreshed yet — using the built-in list. Click Refresh to load models from the Codex CLI.
ai.modelListsHint: Validate the Claude list or refresh the Codex list in
ai.codexStaticHint: Codex does not support dynamic model listing — this list is fixed.
ai.permissionHint: How tool calls are gated (Claude & Codex). "Ask via UI" surfaces each request in a modal; "Bypass all" skips the modal — fast, but unsafe outside trusted directories. You can still override engine, model and permission mode per run on the Run screen.
ai.effortUnsupported: Not taken by this model — the engine default is used
ai.effortNotTaken: The default model takes no effort setting, so the engine decides.
ai.effortHint: How much reasoning the model puts into each answer. Higher effort gives deeper answers but uses more tokens. Applied only when the model supports the level (Codex has no Max); otherwise the model's own default is used.
ai.styleNoneHint: No extra text: the engine answers its own way.
ai.styleHint: Added to the system prompt of new sessions. Write your own styles in

translate.title: Translation
translate.hint: Used for translating highlighted text in the Run AI screen.
translate.modelHint: "Default" → picks a fast model (Claude uses Haiku) for faster translation.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.contextHint: Shows how full the current session's context window is. The bar turns amber past the warn threshold and offers a one-click /compact.
sessions.limitOverrideHint: Leave the override empty to auto-resolve from the model (Claude 200k / 1M, Codex 272k).
sessions.quotaHint: Follows each engine's real subscription plan windows (from /usage): a rolling 5h window and a weekly window (resets per account). With no plan data (e.g. API-key sessions) these settings do nothing.
sessions.quotaWarnHint: Shows a toast once when a 5h or weekly window reaches this percent, and turns the usage badge amber. It never blocks; the toast comes back only after the window resets or drops below.
sessions.blockHint: Checked before each new session and follow-up: Puppeteer blocks it (you can override per turn) when its engine reaches any window set here. Codex usually exposes only the weekly window, so set Weekly to cover it.
sessions.orderHint: Keep the warning below the block thresholds, e.g. warn at 70 and block at 90, so you are warned before you are blocked.
sessions.warnNotBelowBlock: The warning is at or above a block threshold, so that window blocks without warning first. Lower the warning.
sessions.stopRunning: Stop running sessions at the block threshold
sessions.stopRunningHint: When an engine or Claude account reaches a block threshold above, Puppeteer also stops its sessions that are still running, with the reason in each session's log. Sessions on other accounts keep running. When off, only new sessions and follow-ups are blocked.
sessions.stopRunningWarning: A session stopped mid-turn can leave a file half-edited. Check its changes before you continue.
sessions.stopRunningNoBlock: Set a block threshold first: this acts on the 5h or weekly block threshold.
sessions.unattendedHint: Limits for a turn nobody is watching: one a schedule started, or one started from Remote Control. Sessions you start or continue here are not limited. Set them on this computer only: Remote Control cannot change them.
sessions.unattendedMaxTurnsHint: How many times one unattended turn may call the model (each step of tool use is one call). 0 = no limit.
sessions.unattendedMaxMinutesHint: How long one unattended turn may run before Puppeteer stops it. 0 = no limit.
sessions.unattendedStop: A turn that reaches a limit is stopped and marked failed, with the reason in its log and in the notification. It is not resumed on its own: continue it yourself if the work should go on. A long job (a big refactor on a schedule) may need higher limits.

inboxApi.title: Inbox API (Chrome extension)
inboxApi.help: A local HTTP endpoint (127.0.0.1 only) the Chrome extension sends Slack thread links to (/v1/slack-threads). It also offers translation at /v1/translate. Paste the base URL and token into the extension.
inboxApi.enableHint: When off, nothing listens on the port.
inboxApi.remoteDenied: The Inbox API can only be turned on or off on the host itself, not from a remote desktop.
inboxApi.moduleOff: Turn on the Integrations module in Settings → Features first.
inboxApi.regenerateMessage: The current token stops working immediately; the extension must be updated with the new one. Continue?

azure.title: Azure Accounts
azure.intro: Add Azure accounts and link one to each project. Each account is its own az login, isolated and managed by Puppeteer, so several tenants and identities can coexist. az and terraform in runs of a linked project use that account.
azure.isolationWarning: Avoid relying on a global az login for agent work. Puppeteer keeps each account's Azure CLI session in its own directory and points runs at the linked one.
azure.loginExpired: Not signed in, the Azure session expired, or it was signed in without MFA (Azure blocks all write operations). Click "Sign in" to sign in again and complete MFA.
azure.addHint: Adding an account opens your browser for az login. Leave tenant empty to use your home tenant, and subscription empty to use its default subscription.
azure.addWaiting: Complete sign-in in your browser. This waits up to about 5 minutes.
azure.addLoginFailed: Azure sign-in did not complete. If the account now appears in the list, click "Sign in" on it; otherwise add it again.
azure.deleteMessage: Delete this Azure account and its sign-in session? Projects linked to it will be unlinked.

backup.title: File backup
backup.help: Export your whole Puppeteer setup to one file and import it on another machine: app settings, the Skills / Rules library with groups, MCP servers, VPS servers, accounts (GitHub, GitLab, AWS, Azure, Google, Claude), notes / todos and Slack threads (with translations; attachments are downloaded again) and projects (repos, enabled Skills / Rules / groups, MCP and VPS servers, linked accounts). Session history stays on this machine.

export.title: Export
export.includeSecretsHint: PATs, MCP env/header values, Google tokens, SSH passphrases and imported private keys — sealed with your password.
export.passwordWarning: Puppeteer cannot recover this password. Without it the secrets in the file cannot be restored.
export.passwordTooShort: The password must be at least {n} characters.
export.noSecretsHint: Without secrets, accounts must be re-authenticated after import. The file still contains your notes — keep it private.

import.title: Import
import.help: Items are merged by name: matching items are overwritten with the imported version, new ones are added, nothing on this machine is deleted. Replaced Skill / Rule files are moved to the legacy backups.
import.passwordHint: Leave empty to import without secrets.
import.createMissingDirsHint: Paths under the old home folder are moved under this machine's home first. A project whose folder still does not exist gets an empty folder; when this is off, that project is skipped.

report.title: Import result
report.secretsImported: Secrets were restored into the Keychain.
report.reloginHint: Claude and Azure logins never travel: log in to those accounts again, and validate AWS profiles on this machine.

connections.title: Connections
connections.intro: Accounts Puppeteer runs gh, glab, git, aws and az as, and the Google accounts behind its Drive, Gmail and Calendar tools. Open one to validate, edit or delete it.
connections.empty: No connections yet. Add one with “Add connection”.
connections.openHint: Open to validate, edit or delete
